evaluation: ADR completeness + supersession + coherence lint (forge-architect quality gate)

1_adr_completeness.evidence: All 8 carry Context / Decision / Alternatives seriously considered / Consequences / Security notes per docs/adr/0000-adr-template.md:5-9. Alternatives carry real advantages before the loss reason (e.g. ADR-0004:99-105 Unity Cloud Diagnostics 'genuinely close'; ADR-0005:102-110 'loses to calendar and blast radius, not to elegance') — not strawmen. Gap: ADR-0007's Input decision (:87-91) has no rejected alternative (finding F19).

2_status_proposed.evidence: Status: Proposed present on all eight (0002:3, 0003:3, 0004:3, 0005:3, 0006:3, 0007:3, 0008:3, 0009:3). Only ADR-0001 is 'approved', correctly.

3_supersessions_honored.evidence: minSdk 25 pinned (ADR-0004:36,40-42) with AMD-08 cited and verified at EXECUTION_PLAN.md:341-359; 'minSdk 24' appears in ADR-0004 only as the superseded figure (:12,:40,:109). Firebase Crashlytics resolves the architecture.md:24 PIN (ADR-0004:53,56-60), matching EXECUTION_PLAN.md:22. Unity 6000.3.16f1 exact (ADR-0004:32; EXECUTION_PLAN.md:18,439). 8 tps / 125 ms (ADR-0002:30; overview:30,115). No stale value found in the ADR set or overview.md.

4_no_re_derivation.evidence: Three deviations from architecture.md, each declared in the document that makes it: integer-only instead of 'integer/fixed-point' (ADR-0002:88-96, keeps the intent 'no floats'); a 10th asmdef CatMetro.Bootstrap (ADR-0003:27-30,83-90); dotnet-first harness declared as a NEW decision (ADR-0005:3). No locked Global Constraint (EXECUTION_PLAN.md:24-53) is contradicted: catalog, ads-rewarded-only, OneSignal journey budget, 30+10 content, package id, honesty and agent-conduct rules are all either restated or untouched.

5_arch_constants.evidence: ADR-0006:116-165 sets every [ARCH] constant in one file with a per-value rationale, satisfying PRD:88 and PRD:174. But the QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS/QUEUE_MAX_BYTES pair is internally inconsistent with the PRD's own worked instance and with CM-R43.4(a) as written — see finding F1 (blocking).

6_irreversibles.evidence: Explicit 'declare irreversible, human ADR gate' blocks in ADR-0003:122-125, ADR-0006:61,243-249, ADR-0008:163-167; vendor-set freeze ADR-0004:125-128; release path ADR-0009:115-118. Gap: ADR-0002:121-128 uses 'Locked in (hard to reverse)' without the human-gate flag though tick order and digest layout invalidate the whole authored corpus (F20).

7_overview_coherence.evidence: Diagram and ADR-0003's reference table disagree (F12); assembly count wrong (F11); SDK pin count wrong (F14); the CI byte-identity check has no source path in either the content flow or the repo layout (F5).

8_no_invented_sdk_apis.evidence: overview:183-185 disclaims the interface shapes as 'ours' and re-states the never-invent rule (A-07, EXECUTION_PLAN.md:480-481). Named third-party symbols are real and appear in the corpus: BillingClient, Force Resolve, EDM4U (architecture.md:106-114), RC CustomerInfo (risks.md:139), Handheld.Vibrate / VibrationEffect (architecture.md:22), TypeNameHandling / MaxDepth (Newtonsoft), File.Replace (.NET), noEngineReferences (hedged at ADR-0003:53-57). One exception: the directory-fsync step (F7).

findings.issue: QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS=2000 and QUEUE_MAX_BYTES=262144 are deliberately set to bind 'at roughly the same point' (2000 x ~128 B ~= 256 KB, :156-157), but PRD.md:688 CM-R43.4(a) runs the no-loss/no-duplication test with exactly QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS events enqueued. At the cap the byte limit can trip first and oldest-first drops fire (:167-168), so the MUST criterion is flaky-to-unsatisfiable by construction. The stated rationale ('4x the PRD's worked instance of 500 events / 24 h, so the no-loss test runs comfortably below the cap') misreads its own citation: 500/24h is the smoke instance, not the criterion instance.
findings.fix: Give the byte cap headroom against the event cap: set QUEUE_MAX_BYTES >= QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS * QUEUE_EVENT_MAX_BYTES (2000 x 512 = 1 MiB), or lower QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS so 2000 x worst-case serialized size fits inside 256 KiB. Then restate the rationale as 'the event cap is the binding cap; the byte cap is the backstop', and say explicitly that CM-R43.4(a) is run at QUEUE_MAX_EVENTS with the 500/24h smoke instance as the fast variant.

findings.issue: CatMetro.Tests.csproj links unity/Assets/Tests/EditMode/**/*.cs unconditionally, while the same ADR says the Unity EditMode leg covers 'anything needing UnityEngine types' (:93). The first EditMode test that touches UnityEngine or [UnityTest]/UnityEngine.TestTools breaks the dotnet build — i.e. breaks the credential-free required `ci` check (ADR-0009:33) — for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
findings.fix: Split the EditMode tree: unity/Assets/Tests/EditMode/Pure/** (linked by the csproj, engine-free, enforced by the same banned-symbol check as Domain) and unity/Assets/Tests/EditMode/Engine/** (Unity-only, never linked). State the split in the layout block and add it to the asmdef<->csproj parity check in `ci`.

findings.issue: No assembly is assigned as the implementer of ISave, and no storage-root abstraction exists. CatMetro.Application is declared engine-free (:37,:53), yet the save path on Android comes from UnityEngine.Application.persistentDataPath. The same problem was solved for reads with IContentSource (:70-74) and left unsolved for writes; as written, either ISave has no home or CatMetro.Application acquires an engine reference and rule 2 collapses (which would also break ADR-0005's dotnet leg and ADR-0006's claim that the kill-during-write and migration tests run engine-free).
findings.fix: Add the symmetric abstraction (e.g. IStorageRoot { string SaveDirectory; string CacheDirectory; }) to the CatMetro.Services set, note it as a third architect addition with its named requirement, have CatMetro.Bootstrap supply persistentDataPath, and name the assembly that implements ISave (Application, given a root) in ADR-0003's table and overview.md §5.

findings.issue: android-smoke is triggered 'nightly + pre-gate', yet the same section asserts 'A red android-smoke run blocks merge (docs/prd/PRD.md:830)'. PRD.md:830 is a MUST criterion whose text is 'a red smoke run blocks merge'; a nightly job cannot block the merge that broke it. The alternatives section argues for keeping it off per-PR (:97-100) without recording that this weakens a MUST or escalating it.
findings.fix: Either (a) run android-smoke on PRs touching unity/**, content/** and the sim (with the nightly retained for the full AVD matrix), or (b) state plainly that CM-R52.6's merge-blocking reading is narrowed to 'blocks the next merge and the release gate; main is pinned until green', record it as a deviation from PRD.md:830, and escalate it as a human decision alongside NEW-Q48.

findings.issue: The required `ci` check asserts 'config/runtime_bounds.json <-> StreamingAssets byte-identity', but neither ADR-0008's content flow nor overview.md §7's StreamingAssets listing places runtime_bounds.json under StreamingAssets, and catalog.json's per-file SHA-256 index does not cover it. The check has no defined source path, so it cannot be implemented as written.
findings.fix: Add unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/config/runtime_bounds.json to ADR-0008's flow diagram and to overview.md §7, state whether it is listed in catalog.json (and therefore folded into content.sha256), and name the copy step that produces it.

findings.issue: Cause-attribution is 'implemented as <= C such re-runs, where C = distinct routing decisions in the trailing 24 ticks', and C is never bounded by a number. The schema allows switches maxItems 10 (docs/plan/data/level_schema.json:81) over a 24-tick window, so C can reach the low hundreds; at timeLimitTicks max 4000 (level_schema.json:125) that is ~10^6 tick-steps against the 3 s ghost-replay budget (PRD.md:311). The security note claims the work is 'bounded by the 24-tick candidate window', which bounds the window but not the re-run count. The ADR then defers the number to the implementer.
findings.fix: Pin ATTRIBUTION_MAX_RESIMS in config/runtime_bounds.json (ADR-0006 §4) and make the 'camera on the node, zero blame chips' path (PRD.md:310) a hard trigger at the cap rather than a judgement call. State the derived worst case (C_max = switch count x 24) in the security note.

findings.issue: 'serialize -> write save.dat.tmp -> flush/fsync -> File.Replace/rename -> (best effort) fsync the directory'. Managed .NET (and Unity/IL2CPP on Android) exposes no API to fsync a directory entry; an implementer following this step will either invent one or add JNI for it. This is the one place the ADR set names an operation with no platform API behind it.
findings.fix: Specify what is actually reachable: FileStream.Flush(flushToDisk: true) on the temp file before close, then File.Replace (or File.Move with overwrite), and state explicitly that directory-entry durability is not obtainable from managed code and is therefore not part of the guarantee — the .bak fallback is what covers that residual.

findings.issue: Pin hygiene item 1 says versions live in 'exactly two machine-readable places' (unity/Packages/manifest.json + ProjectVersion.txt) and that a [CI] check asserts them against config/pins.json. That excludes the entire dotnet leg: NUnit, NUnit3TestAdapter, the Newtonsoft NuGet package and the .NET SDK 8 requirement have no pin row, while ADR-0005:172-174 requires exactly-pinned versions and a committed lock file. Two ADRs give two different definitions of 'the pinned set'.
findings.fix: Add a third machine-readable location (dotnet/**/*.csproj + packages.lock.json) to ADR-0004 pin hygiene item 1, add pin rows for the NuGet packages and the SDK band to config/pins.json, and extend the `ci` assertion in ADR-0009:33 to cover the lock file.

findings.issue: The v1 payload is declared IRREVERSIBLE and 'the key set and nesting are an irreversible contract' (:83-85), but three sub-objects have no specified shape: caps.counters ({ }), flags ({ }) and breadcrumbs.purchase (null). An irreversible contract with unspecified sub-shapes is not pinned — the first implementer choice becomes the contract without a human gate.
findings.fix: Enumerate them in §2: the five cap counter keys from the locked ad surfaces (rewind_failure, double_tickets, daily_gift_double, streak_saver, theme_rental — EXECUTION_PLAN.md:35-37), the six flag keys already listed at ADR-0007:48-49, and the fields of breadcrumbs.purchase (productId, placement, startedAtUtc, state). Anything left open should be named as open, not rendered as an empty object.

findings.issue: §1 opens 'One file, save.dat, written atomically', while the security notes say 'the offline queue is a separate, metrics-only file with its own bounds'. The queue file is never named, and its path, format, atomicity and backup-exclusion posture are unspecified. The §Open conflict analysis of options A/B/C (:180-195) also reasons as if only save.dat exists, so the backup decision is being escalated with an incomplete file inventory.
findings.fix: Name the queue file in §4 (e.g. analytics_queue.dat), state its format, that it is written outside the save's atomic write, that it is never durable-transactional with the ledger, and fold it into the option A/B/C backup analysis.

findings.issue: '10 asmdefs' contradicts ADR-0003:32-46, which lists 13 assemblies (9 spec rows with Integrations.* expanded into four, plus Bootstrap, plus Editor and two test asmdefs), and contradicts overview.md's own diagram (11 non-test nodes).
findings.fix: State it as ADR-0003 does: '13 assemblies (the 9 spec rows, Integrations.* expanded to four, plus CatMetro.Bootstrap), inward-only, SDKs visible to one assembly'.

findings.issue: The mermaid graph is missing reference edges that ADR-0003's table grants: Services -> Content (ADR-0003:36), Presentation -> Content and Presentation -> Domain (:38), Editor -> Services (:44). A reader validating the dependency rule against the diagram will derive a narrower rule than the one the asmdefs will encode.
findings.fix: Add the four edges, or add a stated convention line ('transitive/read-only-type edges omitted for readability; ADR-0003's table is normative') — the diagram is the artifact reviewers will use, so it should not be quietly stricter than the rule.

findings.issue: The engine/toolchain table row labelled 'API level' carries the value '.NET Standard 2.1 scripting profile'. Two rows later, 'Android | minSdk 25 / targetSdk 36' is the real API-level row. In the one document whose job is to make the API 24 -> 25 supersession binding, an 'API level' row that means something else is a live misreading risk.
findings.fix: Rename the row to 'Scripting API compatibility level'.

findings.issue: '5 pinned SDKs' does not match ADR-0004:46-54, which pins seven rows (purchases-unity+RevenueCatUI, OneSignal, GMA, EDM4U, AppLovin MAX fallback, Firebase Crashlytics, Newtonsoft.Json).
findings.fix: Say 'the 7-row SDK pin table (incl. the dormant AppLovin fallback)' or count only shipped-by-default SDKs and say so.

findings.issue: 'netstandard2.1 occasionally bites (no Span-heavy modern APIs, older BCL surface)' is wrong about Span: netstandard2.1 includes System.Span<T>/ReadOnlySpan<T>/Memory<T>, which ADR-0002:33,52-53 and ADR-0008:53 require in public signatures (Step(ref, ReadOnlySpan<Command>), WriteDigest(Span<byte>), ReadOnlyMemory<T> DTO views). As written it invites an implementer to avoid the exact types the other ADRs mandate.
findings.fix: Reword to name the real gap — netstandard2.1 lacks the .NET Core 3.0+ additions (e.g. newer System.Text.Json, IAsyncEnumerable-adjacent surface, some MemoryMarshal/BitOperations members) — and state that Span/ReadOnlySpan/Memory are available and are the intended vocabulary.

findings.issue: Three off-by-one citations in load-bearing places. ADR-0008 cites docs/prd/PRD.md:734 for the <=200 ms boot validation budget; that criterion is PRD.md:733 (734 is CM-R46.5, the weekday difficulty ramp). ADR-0005 cites EXECUTION_PLAN.md:527 for 'Unity -batchmode -runTests'; it is :526. ADR-0009 cites EXECUTION_PLAN.md:95 for 'Codemagic CI 500 free min/mo'; it is :94.

The context line says the corpus is '30 campaign levels + 10 Night Harbor + 30 pre-validated dailies', conflating the 30-board dated backup pool with the daily pipeline, which pre-validates 90 dates in CI (:32; ADR-0009:35; PRD.md:728).
findings.fix: Rewrite as '30 campaign + 10 Night Harbor levels, 90 daily dates pre-validated in CI, and a 30-board dated backup pool shipped in the build'.

findings.issue: Three different level counts across the set: '40 shipped levels + 30 pre-validated dailies' (0002), '~50 levels of JSON' (0007), '70 levels of progress' in the SAVE_MAX_BYTES model (0006). The save-size model is a load-bearing number and its basis is unstated.
findings.fix: State the basis once (40 shipped at 1.0, up to 60 post-event per EXECUTION_PLAN.md:42-43, plus a 30-board backup pool that produces daily keys rather than per-level progress rows) and make ADR-0006:141-145 cite it.

findings.issue: ADR-0007 bundles nine ratified decisions and supplies a rejected alternative for eight of them. Input (Unity Input System, tap/pointer only) has none — the legacy Input Manager is never weighed, so per the template (docs/adr/0000-adr-template.md:7) that row is a restatement rather than a decision.
findings.fix: Add the legacy Input Manager alternative with its real advantage (zero package, simplest possible tap read) and why it loses (EnhancedTouch multi-safe hit tests per architecture.md:13, new-project default), or mark the row explicitly as ratified-with-no-live-alternative.

findings.issue: ADR-0002 uses 'Locked in (hard to reverse)' where ADR-0003:122, ADR-0006:243 and ADR-0008:163 use 'declare irreversible, human ADR gate'. Per-tick order and digest layout invalidate every authored level and every checked-in golden — the sharpest irreversibles in the set — so the weaker phrasing under-signals them relative to its siblings.
findings.fix: Use the same 'declare irreversible — human ADR gate' heading in ADR-0002 for the tick order and the digest layout, and cross-reference the golden-regeneration rule at ADR-0009:66-69.

findings.issue: AGENTS.md still records 'Stack: TBD — deferred until the product specs land' with a stack-agnostic gate harness, while ADR-0004 pins Unity/IL2CPP/.NET Standard 2.1 and ADR-0005 changes what scripts/check.sh and scripts/test.sh actually run. No ADR names the AGENTS.md update as a consequence, so ratifying this set leaves the repo's own instruction file contradicting it.
findings.fix: Add to ADR-0004 Consequences (and overview.md §7): 'ratification updates AGENTS.md's Stack line to Unity 6000.3.16f1 / C# / IL2CPP and records that check.sh/test.sh now route to the dotnet leg (ADR-0005)'.
